dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?

Hi hon, Tony, good morning. It's Kwame Kim. Listen, I got my water and sewer bill again and it's higher than the last one, and the last one was already higher than the one before. I don't get it. Every quarter it goes up and I'm one person in that apartment.
Okay, Mr. Kim, I'm sorry about that. Let me pull up your account. Can you give me the name it's under and the service address?
Kwame Kim, K-W-A-M-E, Kim like it sounds. And the address, I'd rather not say it over the phone, you can find me by the name, can't you?
I can try by name. Give me a second. [pause] Okay, I've got a Kwame Kim here, renter on the account. Is the phone on file ending in zero one seven three?
That's me, that's the landline. Same number since forever.

Good. So I'm looking at the last three bills. The usage did climb. This latest one covers a longer stretch of days than the one before, and that happens sometimes with the reading schedule. So part of the jump is just more days billed.
More days. Hon, I didn't use more days, I used the same days. Nobody ever told me that. Every time I call it's something new.

I hear you. The meter reading date moves a little and the billing period stretches. The consumption figure is what the meter shows, and I can see it's up some. A running toilet or a leak can do that too. Have you noticed anything running?

The toilet runs sometimes, I jiggle the handle. I told the landlord twice. Twice! Nothing. Anyway, that's not why I called, well, it is, but I got other things. Can I change where you mail the bill? I want it to go to my niece's place, she helps me with the paperwork, and I want to go paperless too, the email thing.
Sure, we can do both. For the mailing address I'll need the new street address, city, and zip. For paperless, I'd need an email address to attach to the account.
Okay, hold on, let me get the paper. [pause] Here. It's forty-one Harbor Court, Middletown, zero two eight four two. Is that right, Middletown, same as Newport, no? No, it's different, I know that.
Different town, but we can mail there. Forty-one Harbor Court, Middletown, oh-two-eight-four-two. Got it. And the email?
Now that one I don't have in front of me, my niece set it up. Can I give it to you when you call me back? She's coming by tonight.
That works. I'll note the mailing address change now, and we'll hold the paperless switch until you have the email. Just so you know, the bill will keep coming on paper until that's added.
Fine, fine. Now here's the real thing. This bill, I can't swing it all at once. Is there a payment plan? Can I pay it in pieces? I'm on a fixed income, hon, and the heating oil already ate my month.

That's a fair question. There are sometimes arrangements for spreading out a balance, but the details, like how many installments and what the terms are, I'd have to confirm with the supervisor in billing. I don't want to hand you the wrong terms.
So you can't tell me yes or no.
Not right this minute. I'll ask her this morning, and I'll also ask whether the longer billing period can be looked at. Can I call you back on the landline?
Yes, please call me back, that's what I want. Today if you can, I'm home all afternoon. Well, I go out for a bit around one, I got a thing at the senior center, but I'm back by three.
Okay. I'll try before one, and if I miss you I'll try again after three. And if I get the answering machine, I'll leave my name and a number to reach billing.

Good, good. You know what, I'm in a good mood about one thing, even with this bill. I finally learned to parallel park. Seventy-something years old and I finally got it, between two cars, first try, down by the library. I was so proud I almost clapped in the car.
Well, congratulations, that's not an easy thing. Good for you.
Thank you, hon. Took me long enough. Okay, back to business, because I'm still not happy. This bill keeps jumping and I want somebody to look at it. Is that what you're going to ask the supervisor?

Yes. I'll ask about the payment plan, and I'll ask if the meter reading and the billing period can be reviewed. I can also put in a note that you've reported the running toilet to your landlord, in case it helps.
Put that in, yes. Twice I told him. Write twice.
Twice, got it. And to be clear, the water and sewer bill is under your name, so the account stays with you even though the mail goes to your niece's.

Right, right, that's fine. She just helps me read the numbers. My eyes aren't what they were. Okay, so mailing address is changed, paperless waits for the email, payment plan question goes to the supervisor, and you call me back. Did I get it all?
You got it all. I'll call you today at the number we have, oh-one-seven-three line, and we'll go from there.
That's the one. Okay Tony, thanks, hon. You were nice about it. Talk later.
You're welcome, Mr. Kim. Talk to you soon. Take care.
